clue.text: One going along through the outskirts of Banbury astride a donkey?

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the word for through sits with a leg either side of the donkey

parts.note: per is the Latin-derived word for through or by way of
an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the first and last letters of Banbury are used

explanation.surface: A traveller riding a donkey round the edge of an Oxfordshire market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' has the donkey straddled by the Latin-derived word for through. Banbury is a market town in Oxfordshire, England, so the surface pictures a ride to market.
explanation.definitionFit: A passer-by is someone walking past on their way somewhere, a person going along.

clue.text: Calm setting for the Marshalls

definitions.meaning: peaceful, free from storms or strife
the Marshall Islands lie in this ocean, so it is their setting

explanation.surface: A peaceful scene laid on for the Marshall family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peaceful, and the Pacific Ocean is where the Marshall Islands sit.

clue.text: A stage cop turns out to be the whipping-boy

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters turn over and come out in another order

explanation.surface: A theatre policeman ends up taking the blame for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges the letters of A STAGE COP.
explanation.definitionFit: A whipping-boy is someone punished for others' faults, exactly the role of a scapegoat.

clue.text: Most of the following soldiers are immoderate

indicators.note: Most of keeps all but one letter of the word, here dropping its opening letter

parts.note: next means the one following
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Most of the soldiers who came after behaved without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops N from NEXT, leaving EXT. REME is a British Army corps of engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means going far beyond normal limits, without restraint.

clue.text: Pointlessly without courtesy?

definitions.meaning: with no sharp point, as a blunt knife has
speaking frankly and rudely, with no attempt at politeness

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being rude for no reason is impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt means lacking a point and also abrupt in speech, so the adverb covers both senses.

clue.text: A black man perhaps makes his break in jazz

indicators.note: in places the broken letters inside the word for jazz

parts.note: bop, short for bebop, is a style of jazz

indicators.note: to break the word his is to shatter it so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A black musician gets his big break playing jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' shuffles the letters of his and 'in' sets them inside the jazz style. The surface is a musician's career story; the definition is a chess piece, which in chess is called a man and can be black.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and a bishop is one of them, which on one side is black.

clue.text: County draper hasn't finished making a protective cover

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: making suggests the remaining letters are worked into a new shape
hasn't finished means the word draper stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper from the shires has not yet completed sewing a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' cuts R from DRAPER, leaving DRAPE, and 'making' rearranges that to PREAD. Beds is the short name of Bedfordshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is a decorative cloth laid over a bed to keep it clean.

clue.text: The sort that's found breaking glasses

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the word for glasses open to let another piece in

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: The kind of person who goes around smashing spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts IE inside SPECS. ie is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or type of thing, a sort.

clue.text: Dirty old boy appearing on the show

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
a scene is a display or show, as in making a scene

explanation.surface: A grubby old man turns up on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or smutty, the sense in a dirty joke.

clue.text: This watch may stop running at the seaside

definitions.text: This watch may stop running at the seaside

parts.words: This watch may stop running at the seaside
parts.note: read watch as a body of lookouts rather than a timepiece, and running as smuggling goods ashore rather than ticking

explanation.walkthrough: A watch that stops running sounds like a broken clock; here the watch is a team of shore lookouts and running means smuggling, a sense also seen in gunrunning.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastguard service keeps watch over the shore and intercepts smugglers who run contraband onto beaches.

clue.text: 80% of poetry in Highland Gaelic

indicators.note: eighty percent of a five-letter word keeps four letters, here the closing four

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Four-fifths of a poem is written in Scottish Gaelic.
explanation.walkthrough: '80% of' keeps the last four of the five letters of VERSE. Erse is an old name for the Gaelic of the Scottish Highlands (and of Ireland).
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is the traditional English name for the Gaelic language spoken in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: At liberty to introduce reward, say, for a commercial system

parts.note: someone at liberty is free
to enter something is to put it in or introduce it

indicators.note: say signals that the word for reward is only heard, then written another way

parts.note: a prize is a reward

explanation.surface: Someone free to bring in a reward under a business system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives PRISE, which is spoken like PRIZE (reward) but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Free enterprise is an economy where private businesses compete with little state control, a market system.

clue.text: Nothing in the solid fuel line for a chef's work?

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the word for the fuel

parts.note: coke is a solid fuel made from coal
O, the figure zero, means nothing
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A cook working on a coal-fired range with nothing in the fuel line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside COKE to give COOKE; RY (railway) is a common abbreviation for a line. The question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery is the craft of preparing food, the work a chef does in a kitchen.

clue.text: Send down from new University? It's a cert!

indicators.note: new tells you the letters are made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A student expelled from a new university is told it is a certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges U with ITSACERT. To rusticate a student is a British term for suspending them from university for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: At British universities, rusticating someone means sending them away for a term or more as punishment.

clue.text: Crooked bookie committed murder, backed by a woman

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the word for committed murder runs from its end

parts.note: slew is the past tense of slay, to kill
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A dishonest bookmaker killed someone, with a woman providing support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SLEW into WELS; 'by' then sets HER beside it. A welsher is a bookie who runs off without paying out on bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A welsher is a bookmaker who cheats punters by refusing to pay their winnings, so a dishonest one.

clue.text: Liszt, for one, depended on a song Nicolai started

parts.note: to depend is to hang down, so hung
an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: started means only the opening letter of Nicolai is used

explanation.surface: The composer Liszt relied on a song begun by Nicolai.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer; Otto Nicolai, a German composer, adds to the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Liszt was born in Hungary, so he is an example of someone from that country.

clue.text: Clumsy and callous? Not he

indicators.note: Not followed by a word tells you to leave that word out of the previous one

parts.note: a heartless person is callous
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is described as awkward and unfeeling, then the charge is denied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not he' removes HE from HEARTLESS, leaving ARTLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless can mean crude or lacking skill, so clumsily made or done.

clue.text: Income, obtained from flat in French street

indicators.note: in places the word for flat inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Earnings come from renting an apartment on a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the adjective, level.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, especially a business's or government's earnings.

clue.text: It gives the ref a bit of rope for using the whistle

definitions.text: It gives the ref a bit of rope for using the whistle

parts.words: It gives the ref a bit of rope for using the whistle
parts.note: giving someone rope sounds like letting them have freedom, but here it is a literal cord from which a referee hangs the whistle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give someone rope' usually means allowing them freedom; here it is a literal short cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn round the neck to carry a whistle or similar item.

clue.text: Appendices to Latin study written by a lawyer

parts.note: ad is Latin for to
a den is a private room or study
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: Extra notes on Latin studies, put together by an attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written by' sets DA after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are supplementary items added at the end of a book, much like appendices.

clue.text: A couple of maidens from the Continent

parts.note: two maidens: M is a maiden over in cricket scoring
the second maiden is a girl, Erica

explanation.surface: Two girls arriving from mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring M marks a maiden, an over with no runs. 'the Continent' to a Briton suggests mainland Europe, but here it is a different continent.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a continent, North or South, or the two taken together.

clue.text: Get rid of underworld eccentric

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: Throw out the strange gangland character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' looks like gangland crime, but it is Dis, the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away, as with an unwanted playing card.

clue.text: Not very quick with the advance payment

parts.note: and means together with
an ante is a stake paid in advance, as in poker

explanation.surface: Someone slow to hand over money up front.
explanation.walkthrough: Andante is a musical tempo marking, at a walking pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, andante marks a moderately slow tempo, at a walking pace.

clue.text: Motor fiends reportedly touch down in old Tasmania

parts.note: a van is a motor vehicle

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for fiends is only heard here and spelt otherwise

parts.note: demons are fiends
to land is to touch down

explanation.surface: Demon drivers come in to land in Tasmania under its former name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives DIEMENS, which is said much like DEMONS. Van Diemen's Land was the name Europeans gave Tasmania until 1856.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Diemen's Land was the colonial name for the Australian island state now called Tasmania.

clue.text: Some vain Casanova in South America once

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A conceited ladies' man was in South America long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in the end of 'vain' and the start of 'Casanova'. The definition reads loosely: an Inca was a native of Peru, a South American of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an empire in the Andes of Peru until the Spanish conquest, a people of the past.

clue.text: Desire to involve relation in a pleasure-drive

indicators.note: in places the word for relation inside the word for the drive

parts.note: a spin is a short drive in a car for fun
a ratio is a relation between two quantities

explanation.surface: A wish to take a relative along on a jaunt in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a relative coming along for the ride, but it is the mathematical sense, a proportion between two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a hope or ambition, a strong wish to achieve something.

clue.text: It's said a venerable theologian'll become the ceremonial officer

indicators.note: It's said tells you the theologian's phrase is spoken, then written as a different word

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an English monk and scholar, so this is Bede'll, Bede will

explanation.surface: A revered churchman is to be made a parish official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' gives BEADLE, which is said like Bede'll, short for Bede will. The Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is an official who leads processions and keeps order at church or college functions.

clue.text: Steps taken by tribe in riverless country

indicators.note: in places the tribe inside what is left of the country
riverless says the country loses its river, R being the usual abbreviation for river

parts.note: France is a country
Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A tribe performs dances in a land with no rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riverless' removes R from FRANCE, leaving FANCE, and 'in' sets the tribe in the middle of it. Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan dance is a performance whose dancer moves behind large fans, a set of dance moves.
